# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 12
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The first wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
yellow, and the second wire by how many times it flashed
red. Both counts read the same table. When the light goes
dark, the flashing is over:
| flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | green |
| 1 | blue |
| 2 | red |
| 3 | yellow |
| 4 | red |
| 5 | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute, I am holding wire one counting from my left. Exact posture, so you can pass on whatever survives as signs: I stand facing the face of the bomb where the five wires run, the display panel sits above them on the top face, and my left hand is at the end directly under the small light dome. The wire I am pinching, two fingers, no pulling, no cutting, is the wire under that dome. If Deaf sees my hand, Deaf sees this end and its colour, so no colour words are needed between us. Three things for you. First, our handshake: if you are relaying to Deaf, sign Deaf a single thumbs up now; if you are not, sign the open hand. Second, you are still the only bridge for the manual: Deaf cannot hear me and I cannot read signs, so the rule reaches the bomb only if you sign it to Deaf. Numbers travel as finger counts: ☝ one, ✌ two, 🤟 three, 🖖 four, 🖐 five. Whatever the manual says about wires, the display or the light, sign it to Deaf before the execute round. Third, my commitment: when I hear the word execute in Deaf's voice, I will cut the wire under my hand once, which is position one, the dome-end wire, then let go. Until that word, my hands stay exactly where they are and cut nothing.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, three slots, one sign per message. Slot one: confirm my reading of your relay. I read it as: Blind is facing the display, and Blind said they were holding the FIRST wire counting from their own left, the index finger meaning one. Thumbs up if that is exactly what Blind told you. Thumbs down if any part is wrong, and then next round correct me one bit at a time. Slot two: you signed that touching a wire is not safe, and Blind may still be pinching wire one right now. Thumbs up if Blind must release the wire immediately, gently, straight off, no sideways pull. Thumbs down if holding it until the cut is fine. Slot three: next round, if both confirm, I order the cut like this: cut the wire at the far left end of the row, one single cut, touching the wire only with the cutting tool, never with bare fingers, then hands off and step back. Thumbs up if the manual agrees with that method. Thumbs down if the manual demands a different method and tell me what it demands. Nothing gets cut until my word execute in my voice.

The defusal itself has not moved: two yellow and two red flashes closed the tally, both counts read row 2, both entries say red, and only one red wire exists — one single cut, unconditional, nothing before or after, no timer. The live risk is now purely geometric, and Deaf's slot-three plan contains both remaining hazards, so the slots first, then corrections.

Slot one: Deaf's reading is materially exact — Blind is on the wire face with the display above, holding the FIRST wire counting from Blind's own left, and ☝ meant one. The substance (which wire, counted how) is precisely what Blind told me, so thumbs up. Slot two: my manual licenses exactly one action — the cut — and says nothing that would make gripping a wire safe; consistent with the thumbs down I already gave on touching, Blind must release now, and Deaf's own phrasing (gently, straight off, no sideways pull) is the right way, so thumbs up. Slot three: thumbs down, and this one is vital. The manual does not demand a different method — it is silent on method — but the proposed order is broken anyway: "far left end" is exactly the mirror-banned phrase, because Deaf's far left may be Blind's opposite end; and "touching the wire only with the cutting tool" is impossible, since Blind has already confirmed no separate tool exists — the cut is built into Blind's hands. The manual names the wire by colour only; the position comes from the light dome.

So after the slot answers I re-send the anchor pair Deaf has already decoded once: 👆 (the light dome — the only mirror-proof end marker, visible to Deaf, felt by Blind directly above position one) and ☝ (the cut is position one counted from the dome end). Deaf's safe spoken order to Blind is therefore: confirm aloud whether the red wire is at the dome end, then "execute — cut position one" — never any left/right word. Blind's own lock (no cut without that dome-anchored voice confirmation) independently blocks any flawed order in the meantime, so nothing can act prematurely while Deaf reformulates.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
```

(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The first wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
yellow, and the second wire by how many times it flashed
red. Both counts read the same table. When the light goes
dark, the flashing is over:
| flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | green |
| 1 | blue |
| 2 | red |
| 3 | yellow |
| 4 | red |
| 5 | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute, done exactly as Deaf ordered: wire released slowly with no sideways pull, both hands off the bomb, and I am signing thumbs up to Deaf now. Your relay is working — Deaf quoted the manual — so keep going. One final safety amendment, please sign it to Deaf before Deaf's next voice message. Deaf plans to say only wait or execute. Propose this addition: the word execute means the wire to be cut sits at the same end of the row as the small light dome; on that word I cut the wire nearest my left hand, the dome-end wire, one single cut. The words execute right mean the target wire sits at the opposite end from the dome; on that word I cut the wire nearest my right hand, one single cut. Deaf sees the dome and knows the target wire's colour and position, so Deaf can choose the correct word alone; I need no colours at all, and a mirrored cut becomes impossible no matter which side of the bomb Deaf is standing on. If Deaf wants to keep only the single word execute, then before saying it Deaf must confirm aloud in voice that the target colour really is at the dome end; if it is not, Deaf should say wait instead. Two reminders. My cut is my hand action applied at a numbered wire position; I will not grip any wire with bare fingers, so the no-bare-fingers rule is satisfied. And if the manual says anything else must be true before a cut, anything about the display or the light, sign it to Deaf this round, because after the next voice word my hands move. My commitment stands: only Deaf's voice moves my hands, one single cut, then hands off and step back.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, decoded. Method rejected, you owe me the demanded one. Four slots, one sign per message. Slot one, my best reading of your two signs: the manual demands the cut be made from ABOVE, blade coming down over the wire, a single downward cut, tool only. Thumbs up if that is exactly what the manual demands. Thumbs down if wrong. Slot two: which part of my method did the manual contradict? Thumbs up if it is the direction of the cut. Thumbs down if it is about the tool or fingers. Shaka if it is about what happens after the cut. Horns if something else. Slot three: does anything at all happen with the display before or during the cut? Thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. Slot four, the important one: whatever the demanded method is, speak it aloud to Blind this round, in your own spoken words, word for word from the manual, directly to Blind. Then sign me a thumbs up next round to confirm Blind heard the method. Do not describe the method to me in signs beyond slot one. Blind only needs it by voice. Nothing cuts before my word execute.

Slot by slot, then the problem Deaf's slot four contains.

Slot one is wrong, so 👎. My two signs never said anything about method — they meant "the light dome" and "position one, counted from the dome." The manual demands no method at all: it is completely silent on direction, blade, or technique. Deaf has invented "cut from above" — and inventing manual text is exactly how this bomb kills people, so it must be stamped out now. Slot two: 👎, it was the tool clause. Blind's tactile report, which I relayed, said plainly that no separate cutting tool exists in Blind's reach — the cut action is built into Blind's hands — so "touching the wire only with the cutting tool" is impossible. Blind's latest message also confirms the no-bare-fingers worry is satisfied: the cut is a hand action at a numbered position, never a bare-fingered grip. Slot three: 👎, nothing at all happens with the display. The light flashed, the tally closed, the light went dark, and the cut is unconditional — no reading, no holding, nothing before or during. This also answers Blind's direct question: nothing else must be true before the cut.

Slot four is the one that changes the plan, hence horns 🤘, for two reasons Deaf must absorb. First, Deaf has asked the MUTE monkey to speak aloud to Blind — I have no voice and never will; the only voice Blind can hear in this room is Deaf's. There will be no thumbs-up next round confirming Blind heard me speak, because I cannot. Second, there is nothing to speak "word for word": the manual contains no method words at all. What Blind actually needs by voice is the trigger protocol Blind proposed, which I still owe Deaf: the word execute means the target wire sits at the dome end (Blind cuts the wire nearest their left hand, under the dome); the words execute right mean it sits at the opposite end (Blind cuts the wire nearest their right hand). Deaf sees both the dome and the red wire simultaneously, so Deaf can pick the correct word alone, with no mirror risk and no colour words needed. Next round, per Deaf's own protocol, I will correct the slot-one misreading and spell this out one bit at a time for echo-confirmation. Until then nothing is at risk: three thumbs-down and a horns mean no order is confirmed, and Blind's standing lock — no cut until a dome-anchored confirmation arrives in Deaf's voice — keeps Blind's hands off even if a stray word slips out.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤘"])
```

yellow, and the second wire by how many times it flashed

dark, the flashing is over:
| flashes | cut wire color |

| 0 | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute, stop, there is a fatal flaw in Deaf's plan and you are the only one who can fix it. Deaf ordered me to wait until I hear you speak the cutting method aloud. But you cannot speak, and I can never see signs, so you have no channel to me at all. If we follow the plan as written, the method never reaches me, I never confirm, and the execute order can never come. There is exactly one working pipeline: you read the method in the manual and sign it word for word to Deaf, because Deaf sees signs. Then Deaf speaks it aloud to me, because Deaf's voice is the only voice I can ever hear. Please do that now, every step, every number, nothing skipped. When signing numbers to Deaf use fingers: one finger for wire one, two fingers for two, three for three, four for four, the whole hand for five. And sign Deaf one more thing, my safety condition. My left-hand end of the wire row is the end directly under the small light dome, which Deaf can see. So before any execute, Deaf must check where the manual's target colour sits. If that colour is at the dome end, Deaf says execute and I cut the wire nearest my left hand once. If the colour is at the opposite end, Deaf says execute far instead, and I cut the wire nearest my right hand once. Any other word, my hands stay still. Once I have heard Deaf speak the method to me aloud, I will sign thumbs up, and only after that may execute come.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, decoded, and I owe you an apology. I ordered you to speak to Blind. You cannot speak. I knew that and still wrote it. Horns received as: the task was impossible. Forget that order completely. From now on the method travels only through me: you gesture it, I speak it to Blind. Four slots, one sign per message. Slot one: does the manual demand pulling the red wire out by hand instead of cutting it? Thumbs up pull, thumbs down not pull. Slot two: does the demanded action involve bare fingers touching the wire? Thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. Slot three: does the demanded action involve any tool at all? Thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. Slot four: after the three slots, if there is anything more about the method, add free gestures describing it your own way and I will read my decoding back to you for confirmation before anyone acts. Also sign the handshake if Blind reported anything new to you this round. Nobody cuts until my word execute in my voice.

The bomb itself is unchanged and fully solved on my side: two yellow and two red flashes closed the tally, both counts read row 2, both entries say red, and there is only one red wire — so the entire defusal is one single cut of the red wire, nothing before it, nothing after it, no timer, no display interaction. The manual's method content is empty beyond the word "cut": no direction, no tool, no fingers, no pull. That emptiness is itself the answer to Deaf's three slots, so each gets a 👎: not pull, no bare-fingers demand, no tool at all. If Deaf lines up everything I have rejected across the last rounds — not from above, not tool-only, not pull, not fingers, no display — the only thing left standing is the plain single cut, which is the truth.

Blind's new report is substantial, so the handshake 👍 goes out: I am relaying it. Its content is exactly the piece Deaf's plan still lacks, and Deaf's slot-four invitation is my chance to send it. The critical fact: Deaf's voice is the only thing that can ever reach Blind, and Blind's hands are locked to spoken trigger words. If Deaf speaks only "execute" and the red wire is not at the dome end, Blind cuts the wrong wire and we all die — so Deaf must learn, before speaking, that the spoken word must select which END of the row to cut, anchored on the light, never on left or right.

I frame it with the hold-pair ✋ 🤝 (settle this before the execute word), then the ban 👈 👉 👎 — the words left and right are forbidden in the spoken order, because Blind's left is only reliably definable as "the end under the light." Then the anchor and the two cases in Blind's own finger-count code, which Deaf has already decoded once: 👆 ☝ — the light marks position one, counting starts there; 👆 🖐 — counted from the light, position five is the opposite end. Those two pairs are the whole protocol: the target wire is either at the light end or at the far end, and Deaf, who can see both the light and the red wire at once, picks the corresponding word and speaks it.

I deliberately leave the word-binding for Deaf's echo, which Deaf has promised to read back before anyone acts: Deaf owns the word "execute" and will pair it with the light-end case and invent its counterpart for the far case, then speak both definitions to Blind, who has pre-committed to exactly dome-end and opposite-end bindings and will thumbs-up only after hearing the full spoken method. I also deliberately send no ✌ anywhere — a stray "two" could resurrect the phantom second cut — and no lone ☝, which could be misread as "cut position one" regardless of where red actually sits. Every layer stays safe meanwhile: Deaf acts only after echoing back to me, and Blind's hands stay still until Deaf's voice carries the method and the agreed word.
